name: Grain
recipe:
No in-sandbox lane lands. Grain's COMPILER (grainc) ships ONLY as a native ELF x86-64 binary (verified: grain-v0.7.2 release, 79MB, `file` => "ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64 ... dynamically linked ... stripped"). Release assets are grain-{linux,mac,win}-x64 only — NO .wasm asset exists. The compiler source is OCaml/Reason built with dune/esy (compiler/ dir: grainc/graindoc/grainformat/grainlsp, dune-project, esy.json/esy.lock) — not Lane B (C), not Lane C (bare Rust crate; it's OCaml + needs ocaml/opam/dune toolchain we can't host), not Lane D (not pure-Python, not a QuickJS/esbuild-runnable npm tool — the npm wrapper just downloads/execs the native binary).

IMPORTANT NUANCE on the OUTPUT: Grain's EMITTED modules ARE plain wasm32-wasi that run standalone on wasmtime — this is real and confirmed: (1) compiler CHANGELOG: "Support for more WebAssembly runtimes, including Wasmtime and Wasmer"; (2) CLI flag `--use-start-section` replaces the `_start` export with a WASI start section for direct standalone execution; (3) `--wasi-polyfill` for custom WASI; (4) self-contained runtime in stdlib (stdlib/runtime/{gc.gr,malloc.gr,...}) so no JS host needed. So if we HAD a compiled Grain .wasm, `wasmtime run prog.wasm` would work.

BUT: we cannot produce that .wasm in-sandbox (compiler is native-only, un-buildable here) and NO prebuilt compiled Grain sample .wasm is published anywhere (searched grain-lang/grain repo for extension:wasm => zero; vmware-labs/webassembly-language-runtimes does NOT carry Grain). There is therefore no concrete artifact to land or smoke-test.

If you want this anyway: the only path is to run the native grainc ELF OUTSIDE the sandbox (host-side build step) to emit a .wasm, then drop that .wasm in as the in-sandbox artifact. That violates the no-native-exec model for the toolchain itself.
smoke: No landable smoke exists because no .wasm artifact is producible/available in-sandbox. The ONLY smoke that would pass requires a host-side native compile first: (host, outside sandbox) `./grain-linux-x64 compile --release --use-start-section hello.gr -o hello.wasm` where hello.gr is `module Hello; from "wasi/process" include Process; print("hello from grain")`, THEN (in-sandbox) `wasmtime run hello.wasm` => prints `hello from grain`. The in-sandbox half works; the host-side native-compile half is the disqualifier.
blocker: Grain's compiler ships ONLY as a native ELF x86-64 binary (no .wasm release asset) and its source is OCaml/Reason (dune/esy) — not buildable on any of our in-sandbox lanes (not C, not a bare Rust crate, not Python/QuickJS-JS). No prebuilt compiled Grain .wasm module is published anywhere to smoke-test the output. Grain's EMITTED wasm32-wasi modules do run standalone on wasmtime (confirmed via changelog + --use-start-section + self-contained GC stdlib), but producing one requires running the native compiler outside the sandbox — so the toolchain cannot be hosted in-sandbox and there is no artifact to land.

name: Wuffs
recipe:
Wuffs-the-library ships as a PRE-TRANSPILED single-file C header library (stb-style) at release/c/wuffs-vMAJOR.MINOR.c — NO transpiler, codegen, configure, or make is run by the consumer (BUILD.md: "There's no build step"; transpilation is done by whoever CHECKS IN, not checks out). It is pure standard C99: only <stdint.h>/<inttypes.h>/<stdio.h>/<string.h>. So the C lane just compiles ONE .c file.

Steps:
1. Fetch the amalgamation (verified 200, 3,289,964 bytes for v0.4; v0.3 stable = 1,825,612 bytes at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/wuffs/main/release/c/wuffs-v0.3.c — also verified 200).
2. Inject a tiny stdin->stdout main that uses one module. Recommended modules: BASE + ADLER32/CRC32/DEFLATE/ZLIB/GZIP/BZIP2 (decompressors). Set the config defines BEFORE the include:
   #define WUFFS_IMPLEMENTATION
   #define WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULES
   #define WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__BASE
   #define WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__CRC32
   #include "wuffs-v0.4.c"
   then call e.g. wuffs_crc32__ieee_hasher (zero-alloc, stack-init via wuffs_crc32__ieee_hasher__initialize, then __update_u32 over an input buffer). The hello-wuffs-c/ example (main.c + wuffs-parse.c) is an even simpler self-contained pattern but uses a generated parse.c rather than the release amalgamation — prefer driving the release/c file directly.
3. Compile the single .c with the existing in-sandbox clang.wasm C lane targeting wasm32-wasi, -O2, -DWUFFS_IMPLEMENTATION. No external libs needed for the codec/checksum modules (only the example/imageviewer + sdl examples pull X11/SDL — do NOT use those). mzcat.c is plain-C stdio but #includes the unsupported-snapshot and references Linux seccomp under #if defined(__linux__) (inactive on wasm32-wasi) — usable but pin to wuffs-v0.4.c instead for stability.
4. Run the resulting .wasm under wasmtime, piping bytes on stdin.
smoke:
Build a tiny CRC32 driver that reads stdin and prints the IEEE CRC32 as hex, e.g.:
  printf 'hello' | wasmtime run wuffs-crc32.wasm
Expected output: 3610a686  (the standard CRC-32/IEEE of "hello"). Equivalently for a zlib-decode driver: pipe a small zlib/gzip stream on stdin and assert the decompressed bytes match the original. Exit code 0.

name: J (jsoftware/jsource)
recipe: Source build only (no prebuilt WASI exists — verified absent in vmware-labs/webassembly-language-runtimes and via gh code/repo search). jsrc/ has ~239 plain .c/.h, no yacc/lex/bison (no .y/.l files), and an amalgamation script (make2/build_jamalgam.sh) that just cats .c into jamalgam.c — no codegen tool needed for that. BUT the only wasm build target is EMSCRIPTEN, not wasm32-wasi: build_jamalgam.sh runs `emcc -sWASM=1 -sEMULATE_FUNCTION_POINTER_CASTS=1 -sEXPORTED_FUNCTIONS=[_main] ... -o jamalgam.js -L../mpir/linux/wasm32 -lgmp` -> produces a .js+.wasm browser pair (disqualifies it as-is). To get a standalone wasm32-wasi module you must port: (1) replace MPIR/GMP (jgmp.h, jgmpinit.c, prebuilt emscripten libgmp at mpir/linux/wasm32 — NOT a wasi-sdk lib) with a wasi-sdk-built GMP or disable extended-precision; (2) compile-out native threads (thread.c, mt.c, -pthread) to single-thread; (3) resolve heavy reliance on emscripten's EMULATE_FUNCTION_POINTER_CASTS — J's interpreter dispatch casts function pointers across mismatched signatures, which traps under plain wasm unless tables are normalized. Build the amalgam with wasi-sdk clang (--target=wasm32-wasi -mexec-model=command), inject/keep _main reading J sentences from stdin. This is a real port, not a reshim.
smoke: After a successful wasi-sdk build: `echo "2 3 4 +/ . * 1 1 1" | wasmtime jbk.wasm` — or simpler `printf '2+2\n' | wasmtime j.wasm` should print `4`. A tacit check: `printf '(+/ %% #) 1 2 3 4 5\n' | wasmtime j.wasm` prints `3` (mean). Expected: J evaluates the sentence over stdio and writes the array result to stdout, exit 0.
blocker: No prebuilt wasm32-wasi asset exists (Lane A dead). Official wasm build is emscripten browser-glue (.js+.wasm), links MPIR/GMP, and depends on emscripten-only -sEMULATE_FUNCTION_POINTER_CASTS plus native pthreads. A plain wasm32-wasi port requires swapping GMP to a wasi-sdk build (or disabling extended precision), removing threads, and fixing function-pointer-cast UB in the interpreter dispatch — engine-level work, feasibility unconfirmed without an actual build attempt.

name: PureScript (purs compiler)
recipe: No viable lane. `purs` is a GHC-Haskell/cabal project (verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/purescript/purescript/master/purescript.cabal). Release v0.15.16 ships only NATIVE binaries (linux64/arm64, macos, win64 tar.gz) — NO wasm32-wasi asset. Lane A: vmware-labs/webassembly-language-runtimes covers only php/python/ruby (verified contents listing) — no Haskell, and no other prebuilt purs.wasm exists. Lane B: not C/C++. Lane C: not Rust (not mrustc-buildable). Lane D: not pip/CPython and not a JS/npm tool — purs is the native compiler, not a JS package. GHC does have a wasm32-wasi backend (wasm32-wasi-ghc), so a purs.wasm is THEORETICALLY producible, but only by building purs with the full GHC wasm cross-toolchain (Nix ghc-wasm-meta, hours-long native provision + cabal dep graph of ~50 Haskell pkgs) — outside any of the four hand-off lanes and not a verifiable file-layout recipe.
smoke: If a wasm32-wasi purs.wasm existed: `wasmtime run --dir=. purs.wasm -- compile Main.purs` then esbuild the emitted output/Main/index.js — expected: JS modules under output/, runnable in the QuickJS/esbuild lane. No such .wasm is currently obtainable.
blocker: purs is a GHC-Haskell native binary with a large cabal dependency graph; no prebuilt wasm32-wasi asset exists on any source (project releases ship native-only; vmware-labs has no Haskell). Producing one requires the GHC wasm cross-compiler toolchain (Nix-based, native, multi-hour) — not a C/Rust/Python/JS lane and not a verifiable hand-off recipe. NOTE: PureScript's OUTPUT (JavaScript) does run live in the esbuild/QuickJS lane; only the compiler itself can't run in-sandbox.

name: Dhall
recipe: Rust impl: Nadrieril/dhall-rust (crate `dhall` 0.13.0 / `serde_dhall`). Pure, total evaluator — ideal sandbox shape, and upstream already gates network (reqwest) OUT on wasm32 ("no remote imports on wasm"). Build a tiny binary crate that depends on serde_dhall, reads a .dhall file from stdin/arg, calls serde_dhall::from_str / dhall::Parsed::parse_str + .resolve().typecheck().normalize(), prints the normalized expr. Target wasm32-wasi (NOT wasm32-unknown-unknown). The evaluator does no I/O once imports are local-file-only, so it fits WASI cleanly. CAVEAT for our mrustc lane: dhall-rust pulls dhall_proc_macros (syn 1.0 + quote + proc-macro2), pest + pest_consume (derive proc-macros), AND a build.rs that runs abnf_to_pest + pest_generator to codegen the grammar at build time. mrustc ~1.74 cannot execute proc-macros or build-script codegen of that shape — so Lane C via mrustc is blocked. Only buildable with a real rustc toolchain producing wasm32-wasi. If standard rustc-on-wasm32-wasi is acceptable, this is live; via mrustc it is not.
smoke: printf 'let x = 2 in [ x, x + 3, x * 4 ]' | wasmtime dhall-wasi.wasm  # expect normalized: [ 2, 5, 8 ]  (and `1 + 1` -> 2). Confirms parse+typecheck+normalize with zero network/fs imports.
blocker: No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi asset exists (vmware-labs LR: none; wasmer registry getPackage(dhall)=null; dhall-haskell releases ship only native darwin/linux/windows binaries — Haskell, no clean wasi path; PyPI `dhall` is Rust C-extension bindings, not pure Python). Lane C source (dhall-rust) is proc-macro + build.rs-codegen heavy (syn/quote/proc-macro2, pest derive, abnf_to_pest/pest_generator build script) -> exceeds mrustc ~1.74 ceiling. Buildable only with a real rustc wasm32-wasi toolchain; under our mrustc lane it is impossible. Hence uncertain, not live-likely.

name: Qwik
recipe:
No viable in-sandbox lane. Investigation of @builder.io/qwik@1.20.0 (verified 200, tarball downloaded + extracted):

The only "portable" artifact is the optimizer at package/bindings/qwik_wasm_bg.wasm (3.0M). It is NOT a wasm32-wasi module — it is a wasm-bindgen module. Verified its imports are 100% JS-host functions (__wbg_*, __wbindgen_string_new, __wbindgen_memory, __wbindgen_number_new, etc.) with ZERO wasi_snapshot_preview1 imports. It cannot run under bare wasmtime; it requires a full JS host to supply the wasm-bindgen glue.

The JS glue (package/bindings/qwik.wasm.cjs) confirms it needs WebAssembly.Module / WebAssembly.Instance / WebAssembly.instantiate(Streaming) plus TextEncoder/TextDecoder and fetch — i.e. a Node/browser JS environment that itself embeds a WASM engine. Our in-sandbox JS lane is QuickJS (no WebAssembly global, no nested wasm engine) + esbuild (a bundler, not a JS-with-wasm runtime), so Lane D fails too.

Lane A: no plain wasm32-wasi asset ships — only wasm-bindgen wasm + native .node binaries (qwik.darwin-arm64.node, qwik.linux-x64-gnu.node, qwik.win32-x64-msvc.node). 
Lane B: N/A (Rust/JS project, no self-contained C). 
Lane C: optimizer Rust source is SWC-based AST transform (SWC-scale, proc-macro-heavy) — far exceeds mrustc ~1.74 ceiling.

The Qwik runtime itself is pure JS that targets a BROWSER DOM (resumable hydration) — it has no compile-to-wasm target and no standalone CLI purpose runnable under WASI.
smoke: If a wasm32-wasi build existed, smoke would be: `wasmtime run qwik_optimizer.wasm --transform demo.tsx` and expect emitted segmented JS on stdout. ACTUAL state: `wasmtime run /tmp/qwik-scout/package/bindings/qwik_wasm_bg.wasm` fails — module has no _start and imports unsatisfiable env funcs (__wbindgen_*, __wbg_*), so wasmtime errors with "unknown import: `__wbindgen_string_new` has not been defined". Confirms it is wasm-bindgen, not WASI.
blocker: Optimizer wasm is a wasm-bindgen module (imports are all __wbg_*/__wbindgen_*, zero wasi_snapshot_preview1) requiring a JS host with an embedded WASM engine (WebAssembly.instantiate) — i.e. browser/Node. Our in-sandbox JS lane (QuickJS) has no WebAssembly global and no nested wasm engine, so it can't host the glue either. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi asset exists (404); Rust source is SWC-scale (exceeds mrustc). Runtime is browser-DOM JS with no WASI purpose.

name: SWC (@swc/wasm)
recipe: SWC ships NO plain wasm32-wasi module. The published @swc/wasm@1.15.41 (verified 200, 15MB tarball: wasm.js + wasm_bg.wasm + wasm.d.ts) is a wasm-bindgen build: the .wasm has 0 wasi_snapshot_preview1 imports and 104 __wbindgen imports, no _start. It CANNOT run standalone under wasmtime. It is a pure function (minifySync/parseSync/transformSync/printSync), but it requires a JS host. The wasm.js glue uses require('fs').readFileSync, require('path'), require('util').{TextEncoder,TextDecoder}, and synchronous new WebAssembly.Module/Instance with imports={__wbindgen_placeholder__:...}. So the ONLY in-sandbox path is our JS lane (QuickJS-ng / esbuild-Node-shim, epic wb-spy): load package/wasm.js as a CommonJS module, providing (1) the WebAssembly JS API, (2) Node fs/path/util shims (we already have these from wb-spy), then call exports.minifySync(code, opts) / transformSync. Lane A impossible (no WASI asset exists, vmware-labs WLR has none). Lane C impossible (SWC is a huge proc-macro-heavy cargo workspace, far past mrustc 1.74). The hard gate: QuickJS-ng does NOT implement the WebAssembly global by default — must confirm/enable WASM-in-JS support in our QuickJS host (or fall to a WebAssembly polyfill, which would defeat native-fast JIT). esbuild lane is JS-bundler only, cannot host a .wasm at runtime.
smoke: In our in-sandbox JS host (QuickJS-ng with wb-spy Node shims), run: `node -e "const swc=require('@swc/wasm'); console.log(swc.minifySync('const x = 1 + 2; console.log(x);', {compress:true,mangle:true}).code)"` — expect minified output like `console.log(3);` (or `const x=3;console.log(x);`). PRECHECK first: `globalThis.WebAssembly` must be defined in the QuickJS host (`node -e "console.log(typeof WebAssembly)"` -> "object"); if "undefined", that is the blocker and the smoke will throw at module load (new WebAssembly.Module).
blocker: No WASI build exists — only wasm-bindgen (JS-host, 0 wasi imports / 104 wbindgen imports). Lanes A/B/C ruled out. Lane D viability hinges on our QuickJS-ng host exposing the WebAssembly JS API (Module/Instance/imports). QuickJS-ng does not enable WebAssembly by default; unconfirmed whether our build does. If absent, no clean path without a WASM-in-JS polyfill (which loses the native-JIT benefit). Node fs/path/util shims are already covered by wb-spy.

name: Rollup (@rollup/wasm-node)
recipe: @rollup/wasm-node is NOT a standalone WASI module. Verified by unpacking the 4.61.1 tarball: dist/wasm-node/bindings_wasm_bg.wasm is a wasm-bindgen module whose ONLY imports are JS glue ("./bindings_wasm_bg.js") with ZERO WASI imports (no fd_write/proc_exit/wasi), and whose only exports are `parse` + `xxhash*` — i.e. just the SWC-based AST parser/hasher, not the bundler. All actual bundling (module-graph, tree-shaking, codegen, fs I/O, plugins, config loading) lives in PLAIN Node JavaScript (dist/rollup.js, dist/shared/*.js, dist/bin/rollup, loadConfigFile.js, fsevents-importer.js). So it requires a Node JS host + wasm-bindgen JS glue; it cannot run under bare wasmtime. The only in-sandbox path is our QuickJS/esbuild JS lane (Lane D): vendor the npm package + its bindings_wasm.js glue and run dist/bin/rollup on a Node-compatible JS runtime, brokering fs via JsDock. NOTE: rollup's CLI uses Node fs/path/url/events plus dynamic config loading — QuickJS shim coverage (Node compat) is the real gate; esbuild already covers most bundling needs we'd use this for, so Rollup-on-QuickJS is low-value vs effort.
smoke: Negative smoke proving it is NOT WASI (run from unpacked tarball): `wasm-tools print package/dist/wasm-node/bindings_wasm_bg.wasm | grep -ciE 'wasi|fd_write|proc_exit'` -> expect `0`; and `wasm-tools print ... | grep -oE '\(import "[^"]+"' | sort -u` -> only `(import "./bindings_wasm_bg.js"`. Attempting `wasmtime run bindings_wasm_bg.wasm` fails: it has no _start/WASI command export and unresolved JS-glue imports. Positive (Lane D, if QuickJS Node-compat is wired): `node-compat-rt dist/bin/rollup main.js --format es -o out.js` over a 2-file input -> out.js contains the merged tree-shaken ESM.
blocker: No standalone WASI lane exists. The shipped .wasm is a wasm-bindgen JS-host module (zero WASI imports, imports only ./bindings_wasm_bg.js) that contains ONLY the SWC parser+xxhash — not the bundler. Bundling is implemented in plain Node JavaScript and requires a full JS runtime + Node fs/path/url/events, so it cannot run under bare wasmtime. Only viable in-sandbox path is the QuickJS/esbuild JS lane (Lane D), gated on Node-API shim coverage — and largely redundant with esbuild.

name: Microbundle
recipe: JS npm lane (NOT a .wasm). microbundle 0.15.1 is pure JS; bin = dist/cli.js, main = dist/microbundle.js. Pinned deps are all pure-JS npm: rollup ^2.35.1 (CRITICAL: rollup 2 = 100% JS, zero deps, only optional fsevents for --watch; the native @rollup/rollup-* binaries only exist in rollup 4 — do NOT let the resolver float to rollup 4), terser ^5 (pure JS: acorn+commander+source-map), @babel/core + presets/plugins (pure JS), postcss/autoprefixer (pure JS), rollup plugins (commonjs/node-resolve/json/alias/babel — pure JS), brotli-size/gzip-size (pure JS, dep duplexer), sade/kleur/tiny-glob/filesize/camelcase (pure JS). Wire-up: install the package + lockfile pinning rollup to the 2.x line (avoid 4.x native), strip optional fsevents (macOS-only file watcher, --watch path only — not needed for one-shot build), bundle the ~40-pkg transitive graph through our npm bundle step (wb-spy), run dist/cli.js under QuickJS with the Node shims (fs/path/process/url) + JsDock fs (reads entry, writes dist/). No native addon, no gyp, no JIT, no network-as-purpose, no GPU, no browser host.
smoke: In a temp dir: write package.json {"name":"t","source":"index.js","main":"dist/t.js","module":"dist/t.mjs"} + index.js `export const add=(a,b)=>a+b;`. Run `microbundle build --no-compress` via the JS lane (node dist/cli.js build). Expect: process exits 0; dist/t.js and dist/t.mjs created containing a minified/transpiled `add` export (e.g. grep dist/t.js for "add"). Expected stdout: a build summary table listing output files + sizes.
blocker: Not a prebuilt wasm — runs only on our in-sandbox JS/npm lane (wb-spy: QuickJS + Node shims + JsDock fs). Two wire-up risks: (1) resolver must pin rollup to 2.x — rollup 4 ships native per-arch binaries that would break wasm; (2) large ~40-package transitive dynamic-require graph (babel/rollup/terser/postcss) must bundle cleanly for QuickJS. Heavy CJS dynamic require + plugin graph means it's 'wire-up + bundle-graph-validate', not a drop-in. Live-likely once the bundle is built and rollup stays on 2.x; uncertain until that bundle is proven to load under QuickJS.

name: Boa
recipe: No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi asset exists. `gh api repos/boa-dev/boa/releases` returns ONLY native binaries (boa-aarch64-apple-darwin, boa-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, boa-*-windows-msvc.exe) across all tags incl v0.21.1 and nightly — no .wasm, so Lane A is out. Boa is pure-Rust (no JIT, no native threads in core engine), so the intended path is `rustc --target wasm32-wasip1` on the real toolchain: build the `boa_cli` bin (cli/src/main.rs, default-run "boa") or a tiny embed using boa_engine::Context. But our in-sandbox compiler lane is mrustc ~1.74, and Boa's workspace declares edition=2024 and rust-version=1.91.0 (workspace.package in root Cargo.toml), with boa_engine pulling boa_macros (proc-macro), the full ICU4X stack (icu_normalizer/icu_locale/icu_datetime/...), yoke/zerofrom derives, NaN-boxing. 2024-edition syntax + 1.91 MSRV + proc-macros are unparseable/unsupported by mrustc. To ship it you must build with stock rustc (add wasm32-wasip1 target, disable cli `fast-allocator`+`fetch` and `intl_bundled` to drop jemalloc/reqwest/heavy ICU), not via our mrustc sandbox lane.
smoke: With a real rustc wasm build: `wasmtime run boa.wasm -- --help` or pipe `echo "console.log(1+2)" | wasmtime run boa.wasm` -> prints 3. (Core eval path needs no fetch/threads/GPU.)
blocker: No prebuilt wasm32-wasi asset (Lane A absent). Lane C (mrustc ~1.74) cannot build it: Boa is edition=2024, MSRV 1.91.0, proc-macro-heavy (boa_macros + ICU4X yoke/zerofrom derives) — beyond mrustc's ceiling. It WOULD build cleanly on stock rustc for wasm32-wasip1 (pure Rust, no JIT), but that's outside our mrustc-only in-sandbox lane.

name: pnpm
recipe: No viable lane. Lane A: pnpm v11.6.0 release ships ONLY native per-platform binaries (pnpm-{darwin,linux,win32}-{x64,arm64}[-musl].{tar.gz,zip}) plus the npm tarball (registry.npmjs.org/pnpm/-/pnpm-11.6.0.tgz, bin/pnpm.mjs -> bundled dist/pnpm.cjs). No wasm32-wasi asset exists anywhere (no vmware-labs WLR, no wasmer/wapm pkg). Lane D (Node-shim/QuickJS): pnpm is pure-JS but engines requires node>=22.13, single ~megabyte bundled CJS that reaches deep Node internals incompatible with our QuickJS/Node-shim lane: worker_threads (parallel resolution/install workers), child_process (lifecycle scripts + git/tarball deps, bundles node-gyp), and — disqualifying — its WHOLE PURPOSE is (1) live HTTP fetching from the npm registry [real-networking-as-purpose] and (2) a content-addressed store built on filesystem HARDLINKS/SYMLINKS (fs.link), which WASI preview1 does not expose. Lanes B/C N/A (not C/Rust). Per scout rules, real-networking-as-purpose => impossible.
smoke: N/A — no buildable artifact. If forced to demonstrate the blocker: under any WASI host, `fs.linkSync(a,b)` throws ENOSYS (WASI preview1 has no path_link symlink/hardlink store semantics), and the registry fetch has no socket. Expected: pnpm aborts before resolving a single package.
blocker: pnpm's core purpose is real networking (live npm-registry HTTP fetch) + a hardlink/symlink content-addressed store (fs.link) that WASI fs doesn't provide; also needs node>=22.13, worker_threads, child_process (node-gyp). No prebuilt wasm32-wasi asset exists. Cannot run as a standalone WASI module under wasmtime with no native exec / no JS-net host.

name: Zig build / zigmod
recipe: No viable lane. zigmod is written in Zig (not C/Rust/Python/JS), so Lanes B/C/D are N/A. Lane A: release r104 (latest, verified via gh api) ships ONLY native binaries — zigmod-{aarch64,x86_64}-{linux,macos}, plus mips64el/ppc64le/riscv64-linux. No .wasm asset exists; vmware-labs/webassembly-language-runtimes (HTTP 200, exists) carries C/Python/Ruby/etc., not zigmod. The only conceivable path is compiling zigmod from source to wasm32-wasi via our Zig lane, which is not feasible: (1) zig.mod sets min_zig_version 0.16.0 (bleeding-edge unreleased Zig, beyond our lane); (2) build is circular — min_zigmod_version r96, deps.zig is generated by zigmod fetching 13+ git deps, and build.zig runs `git describe` via b.run at build time; (3) links system libc + pulls zigwin32; (4) src/main.zig is built on std.Io.Threaded (native threads) — unavailable on single-threaded wasm32-wasi.
smoke: N/A — nothing to smoke-test. If one nevertheless tried `zig build` against the source, it would fail at dep resolution (needs zigmod itself + network git-clone of nektro/zig-* repos) before producing any wasm. Even a hypothetical wasm32-wasi binary would no-op: `zigmod fetch` requires git-clone + HTTP to remote registries, which the no-real-networking sandbox cannot provide.
blocker: Network-as-purpose: zigmod's core function is git-cloning + HTTP-fetching remote Zig packages (deps zig-git, zig-nio/nfs) — dead in a no-real-networking sandbox. Plus native-threads runtime (std.Io.Threaded), circular self-bootstrap (min_zigmod_version r96 + build-time git describe), system libc, and min_zig_version 0.16.0 beyond the Zig lane. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi asset exists.

name: Binaryen (wasm-opt)
recipe: No working lane. (A) The only prebuilt .wasm is the emscripten/JS build inside binaryen-version_130-node.tar.gz (verified URL 200): tar contents = wasm-opt.wasm + wasm-opt.js. wasm-tools print on wasm-opt.wasm shows minified emscripten imports from module "a" plus an imported SHARED/pthread memory (a A, a a memory ... shared) — it is NOT a plain wasm32-wasi module; it cannot run standalone under wasmtime, it needs the emscripten .js glue + a JS host. No wasmer/wapm package exists (registry getPackage:null). (B) Building from C++ source IS layout-favorable — pre-generated src/gen-s-parser.inc is checked in, config.h.in only templates PROJECT_VERSION (one #define, hand-writable), no bison/flex/yacc, the googletest/fuzztest/mimalloc submodules are test/optional-only, ~227 plain C++17 .cpp under src/, wasm-opt is a clean file-in/file-out CLI (wasm-opt in.wasm -o out.wasm -O2). Threading has a single-thread fallback (src/support/threads.cpp getNumCores returns 1 under no-threads). BUT the hard blocker is C++ exceptions (see blocker).
smoke: If a wasi build existed: wasmtime run --dir=. wasm-opt.wasm -- in.wasm -o out.wasm -O2 && wasm-tools validate out.wasm  -> exit 0, out.wasm smaller/valid. Cannot be achieved on our lane today.
blocker: C++ exceptions are load-bearing and cannot be compiled out. Upstream issue WebAssembly/binaryen#5206 "standalone (non-js) binaryen.wasm" is still OPEN (since 2022); the contributor who tried wasi-sdk reported: threads are workable, but there is "heavy use of exceptions ... notably parsing, which can't really be worked around without significant changes including to function signatures ... we'd need to wait for wasi-sdk and runtimes to support the exceptions proposal to build." Our wasmtime + clang.wasm lane has no C++ exception-handling runtime (the wasm EH proposal), so the parser cannot be built. The note's claim that it "compiles to wasip1 cleanly" is contradicted by upstream. The only shipped wasm artifact is emscripten+JS (browser/Node host), which our no-JS-host sandbox cannot run. Re-evaluate only if (a) wasi-sdk EH lands in our compiler lane, or (b) Binaryen refactors the parser off exceptions.

name: protoc
recipe: protoc itself is C++ with no plain wasm32-wasi build (Lanes A/B/C dead — see blocker). Use the pure-JS equivalent instead: npm `protobufjs-cli@2.5.4` ships `pbjs`/`pbts`, a JS-native Protobuf compiler that parses .proto and emits code (json/static-module/proto3/TS) with NO protoc, NO native deps. Runs on our in-sandbox QuickJS/esbuild JS lane. Dep tree is all-JS: chalk, escodegen, espree, estraverse, glob, jsdoc, minimist, tmp (no node-gyp/native). Runtime dep `protobufjs@8.6.3` -> only `long` (pure JS), gypfile None, prebuilt on publish. Register: `npm install protobufjs-cli` in the sandbox JS env, then run `node node_modules/.bin/pbjs ...` (or bundle bin/pbjs via esbuild). For protoc-plugin style flows it also ships `protoc-gen-pbjs`. If you specifically need the C++ `protoc` binary semantics (e.g. third-party gen plugins), that is a separate, harder problem — but for pure proto->code generation pbjs is functionally equivalent and pure-JS. NOTE: it uses CommonJS require + reads .proto from fs; confirm our QuickJS lane provides require + wasi fs (esbuild can pre-bundle to a single CJS/ESM file to drop the require concern).
smoke: printf 'syntax="proto3"; message P { string name=1; int32 id=2; }' > p.proto && node node_modules/.bin/pbjs -t static-module -w commonjs -o out.js p.proto && head -5 out.js  # expect: generated JS module defining message P with encode/decode/create (e.g. a line `$root.P = (function() {`). Exit 0.
blocker: Real C++ `protoc` has no plain wasm32-wasi asset: Lane A — only emscripten LIBRARIES exist (dsyer/protobuf-wasm = libprotobuf.a/libprotoc.a, no standalone binary; kwonoj = emscripten js+wasm; VMware WLR ships no protoc); no protoc.wasm in any wasi registry (confirmed via search + WLR releases). Lane B — protobuf C++ uses Bazel/CMake/autotools + bootstraps descriptor.proto via its own protoc (build-time codegen dependency on protoc itself), so no clean .c+.h inject. Lane C — n/a (C++, not Rust). Chosen Lane D risk: pbjs is functionally-equivalent codegen, NOT byte-identical to C++ protoc output, and uses CJS require + fs reads (pre-bundle via esbuild + ensure wasi fs).

name: LLD (wasm-ld)
recipe: No plain wasm32-wasi prebuilt asset confirmed. The runtime-shape is actually ideal — wasm-ld is the LLVM lld WebAssembly flavor: pure C++, no JIT, no GPU, no network, strict file-in/file-out (objects -> linked .wasm). It would run under standalone wasmtime IF a plain-WASI build existed. But the only known wasm builds are disqualified: (1) Wasmer registry clang/clang+lld uses WASIX/posix_spawn (not plain WASI, wasmer-runtime-specific) — see wasmer.io/posts/clang-in-browser; (2) binji/wasm-clang and Guyutongxue/clangd-in-browser are emscripten builds requiring a JS-host in-memory filesystem + SharedArrayBuffer/pthreads (browser-only, not standalone WASI). wasi-sdk ships wasm-ld only as a NATIVE host binary, not as a .wasm. Lane B is blocked: lld lives in the LLVM monorepo and its build requires CMake + LLVM TableGen (.td -> .inc codegen) + CMake-generated config headers (llvm/Config/*.h, abi-breaking.h), plus a large slice of libLLVM (Support/Object/BinaryFormat/Demangle). That is configure/codegen-class build machinery our in-sandbox compiler lane cannot run. Path to live (out of band, on a provisioned host): build the LLVM monorepo with -DLLVM_DEFAULT_TARGET_TRIPLE=wasm32-wasi using the wasi-sdk as a cross toolchain, target just the lld wasm-ld driver, link against wasi-libc, produce wasm-ld.wasm; then register it. Not buildable from source inside the sandbox.
smoke: Once a plain-WASI wasm-ld.wasm exists: write a tiny object (clang.wasm -c hello.c -o hello.o), then `wasmtime run --dir=. wasm-ld.wasm -- hello.o -o hello.wasm` and expect hello.wasm to be produced and `wasmtime run hello.wasm` to print "hello". Negative check today: `gh release` / `curl -fsIL` find NO plain wasm32-wasi wasm-ld asset; Wasmer's needs WASIX, wasm-clang needs JS-host FS.
blocker: No verified plain wasm32-wasi prebuilt wasm-ld.wasm exists (Wasmer build = WASIX/posix_spawn; wasm-clang/clangd-in-browser = emscripten + JS-host in-memory FS + SharedArrayBuffer). Lane B blocked by LLVM build needing CMake + TableGen codegen + generated config headers (cannot run in sandbox). Runtime model itself is fine (file-in/file-out, no JIT/GPU/net) — blocker is purely build provenance, so produce wasm-ld.wasm out-of-band on a provisioned host via wasi-sdk cross-build, then register.

name: Rome / Biome
recipe: No clean lane delivers a bare wasm32-wasi module. (A) No prebuilt plain WASI .wasm exists: biome GitHub releases ship only native binaries (biome-linux-x64, biome-darwin-arm64, ...); the only wasm is @biomejs/wasm-{nodejs,web,bundler} on npm, which is a wasm-bindgen build — a biome_wasm.js + biome_wasm_bg.wasm pair that imports __wbindgen_* host functions and needs JS glue (confirmed: main=biome_wasm.js, description "WebAssembly bindings to the Biome workspace API"). Not in vmware-labs/webassembly-language-runtimes (NONE) nor Wasmer registry (getPackage null). (B) N/A — Rust, not C. (C) mrustc ~1.74 cannot handle the Biome Cargo workspace: rowan/CST parser, dozens of biome_* crates, heavy serde + proc-macro derive, plus the wasm-bindgen dep that targets JS not WASI — far past the mrustc ceiling. (D) N/A — not Python, not a QuickJS/esbuild-runnable JS tool. The only feasible route (out of scope of these lanes) is compiling biome_cli from source to wasm32-wasip1 via a REAL Rust→wasm toolchain (rustc, not mrustc), stubbing the wasm-bindgen-only crate — that is a from-source rustc build, not a prebuilt asset and not mrustc-buildable.
smoke: If a wasm32-wasip1 biome_cli were built: `wasmtime run --dir=. biome.wasm -- check ./sample.ts` should emit lint/format diagnostics and exit nonzero on issues. The existing npm asset FAILS this: `wasmtime run @biomejs/wasm-nodejs/biome_wasm_bg.wasm` errors with "unknown import: env::__wbindgen_*" (no _start, JS-host module).
blocker: Only wasm shipped is a wasm-bindgen JS-host pair (biome_wasm.js + _bg.wasm) that imports __wbindgen_* and has no _start — won't instantiate under bare wasmtime. No plain wasm32-wasi asset exists anywhere (releases native-only; absent from VMware WLR + Wasmer). Building from source to WASI needs real rustc on a large proc-macro/serde/rowan crate graph that exceeds mrustc ~1.74; the wasm-bindgen crate targets JS not WASI. No clean A/B/C/D lane.

name: flatc
recipe:
flatc is self-contained C++11, fixed explicit source list (NO codegen, NO autotools, NO generated headers missing — reflection_generated.h ships checked-in), pure file-in/file-out, single-threaded. Build via our clang.wasm C++ lane targeting wasm32-wasi.

Fetch source at tag v25.12.19-2026-02-06-03fffb2 (git archive or release tarball: https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/archive/refs/tags/v25.12.19-2026-02-06-03fffb2.tar.gz).

Compile this exact set with -std=c++11 -I include -I . (CMake FlatBuffers_Compiler_SRCS, headers omitted):
  Library: src/file_manager.cpp src/file_name_manager.cpp src/idl_parser.cpp src/idl_gen_text.cpp src/reflection.cpp src/util.cpp
  Codegens: src/idl_gen_binary.cpp src/idl_gen_cpp.cpp src/idl_gen_csharp.cpp src/idl_gen_dart.cpp src/idl_gen_kotlin.cpp src/idl_gen_kotlin_kmp.cpp src/idl_gen_go.cpp src/idl_gen_java.cpp src/idl_gen_ts.cpp src/idl_gen_php.cpp src/idl_gen_python.cpp src/idl_gen_lobster.cpp src/idl_gen_rust.cpp src/idl_gen_fbs.cpp src/idl_gen_grpc.cpp src/idl_gen_json_schema.cpp src/idl_gen_swift.cpp
  Driver/aux: src/flatc.cpp src/flatc_main.cpp src/binary_annotator.cpp src/annotated_binary_text_gen.cpp src/bfbs_gen_lua.cpp src/bfbs_gen_nim.cpp src/code_generators.cpp include/codegen/python.cc grpc/src/compiler/cpp_generator.cc grpc/src/compiler/go_generator.cc grpc/src/compiler/java_generator.cc grpc/src/compiler/python_generator.cc

main() already exists in flatc_main.cpp — NO main injection needed. Link to flatc.wasm. Include dirs: -Iinclude -I. (grpc/src/compiler includes are relative). util.cpp uses <unistd.h>/stat/getcwd — all WASI-provided. No -DFLATBUFFERS_CPP_STD override needed (defaults to 11).
smoke: printf 'table Monster { name:string; hp:short; }\nroot_type Monster;\n' > monster.fbs && wasmtime run --dir=. flatc.wasm -- --cpp monster.fbs && ls monster_generated.h  # expect: monster_generated.h created (generated C++ header). Also `wasmtime run flatc.wasm -- --version` prints e.g. "flatc version 25.12.19".

name: JerryScript
recipe: Lane B (self-contained C, CMake cross-build with wasi-sdk). No prebuilt plain-wasi .wasm exists (vmware-labs WLR has none; project releases are source zips only) -> build from source. Verified facts: (1) v3.0.0 tarball returns 200. (2) All codegen outputs are COMMITTED in-tree: jerry-core/lit/lit-magic-strings.inc.h, lit-unicode-*.inc.h, and jerry-core/include/jerryscript-config.h all present — no gen-strings.py/gen-unicode.py/js2c.py needed at build. (3) ENABLE_AMALGAM defaults OFF, so amalgam.py never runs; the only build-time Python is tools/version.py (pure stdlib, no network/deps). (4) Ships its OWN libm (jerry-math/*.c: acos,asin,atan2,cbrt,ceil,...) so no external libm — ideal for WASI. (5) Port layer is plain POSIX (jerry-port/common + jerry-port/unix: fopen/getc/getenv/clock) which wasi-sdk's libc provides; jerry-main/main-desktop.c is a normal int main(argc,argv) reading a file path or stdin. Recipe: fetch+extract tarball; install wasi-sdk-33 (WASI_SDK_PATH); cmake -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$WASI_SDK_PATH/share/cmake/wasi-sdk.cmake -DENABLE_AMALGAM=OFF -DJERRY_CMDLINE=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=MinSizeRel (or use python tools/build.py --toolchain=<wasi-sdk cmake file>). Output jerry-main/jerry .wasm is a wasip1 module. NOTE: redundant with existing in-sandbox QuickJS lane — same role (bytecode JS interpreter, no JIT); only build if a second tiny-footprint engine is wanted. If the default jerry-port-unix.c trips on a missing POSIX call under wasi-libc (e.g. a tty/clock edge), swap to the minimal jerry-port/common implementation or stub the offending port fn — small, contained.
smoke: printf 'print("hello from jerryscript " + (6*7));' > /tmp/t.js && wasmtime run --dir=/tmp ./build/bin/jerry /tmp/t.js  # expect stdout: hello from jerryscript 42  (jerry registers a print() builtin in the cmdline target; alternatively `wasmtime run jerry --version` prints the 3.0.0 build string)

name: Zend Engine (PHP)
recipe: Prebuilt PLAIN wasm32-wasi PHP CGI binary from VMware Labs WebAssembly Language Runtimes. Two confirmed-live variants at tag php/8.2.6+20230714-11be424: php-cgi-8.2.6-slim.wasm (~6.3MB, leaner ext set) and php-cgi-8.2.6.wasm (~13MB, fuller). The `-wasmedge` variants are wasmedge-specific (SKIP); slim/default are standard WASI and run under stock wasmtime. No JIT (Zend is a bytecode interpreter; only the optional JIT is omitted), no native exec, no browser/JS host, no .js sidecar. Register as a CommandRegistry entry: download the slim .wasm into the toolchain cache, run via wasmtime with a mapped dir so PHP can read the script file. Invocation per WLR README: `wasmtime --mapdir=./::./ -- php-cgi <script.php>` (use --dir/preopen + SCRIPT_FILENAME env in wasmtime CLI/wasmex). CGI binary: emits CGI headers then body on stdout; for plain CLI-style output run a script that echoes. Pin by sha256 (sidecar .sha256sum asset published alongside).
smoke: printf '<?php echo "hello from php ".phpversion()."\n";' > /tmp/t.php && wasmtime run --dir /tmp::/tmp -- php-cgi-8.2.6-slim.wasm /tmp/t.php  → stdout contains CGI headers (e.g. "Content-type: text/html") followed by "hello from php 8.2.6". Quick version probe: `wasmtime run -- php-cgi-8.2.6-slim.wasm -v` → prints "PHP 8.2.6 (cgi-fcgi) ...".

name: Ber/SWI-Prolog VM
recipe:
No viable lane. The only maintained SWI-Prolog wasm port is structurally Emscripten/JS-host-bound, not wasm32-wasi.

Lane A (prebuilt plain wasi .wasm): NONE EXISTS. vmware-labs/webassembly-language-runtimes has no prolog asset (verified via gh api --paginate over all releases: zero matches). The official artifact is the npm `swipl-wasm` package (latest 8.0.0, dist/index.js) = a .js + swipl.wasm Emscripten pair — the explicitly disqualified shape. SWI-Prolog/swipl-wasm repo is archived/superseded (no releases, no tags); wasm now lives in main swipl-devel.

Lane B (self-contained C, inject main): BLOCKED. swipl-devel's wasm target is hard-wired to Emscripten in cmake/port/Emscripten.cmake: SWIPL_ARCH="wasm-emscripten", SRC_OS_SPECIFIC=wasm/pl-wasm.c, a WASM_PRELOAD_DIR using Emscripten's preload-file MEMFS to ship the Prolog bootstrap/library (boot .qlf + library/*.pl) into the FS, and Emscripten-only flags -fwasm-exceptions / -sSUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm (engine relies on asyncify + wasm longjmp for its yield/exception model). src/wasm/pl-wasm.c contains 6 EM_JS/EM_ASM bridges that call directly into the JavaScript host for I/O and engine control. Beyond that, building swipl needs a full CMake configure + a native bootstrap compiler step (it bootstraps boot.prc by running a Prolog binary) and a zlib dependency built via emconfigure — i.e. autotools/CMake codegen + a host toolchain we cannot run. No config.h.generic / pre-gen path for wasm.

Lane C (mrustc Rust): N/A — C codebase, no Rust crate.
Lane D (pure-Python / JS-on-QuickJS): N/A. swipl.wasm is not pure-Python and is not a QuickJS/esbuild-runnable JS tool — it is an Emscripten module requiring a full Emscripten JS runtime (FS, asyncify, longjmp shims) that QuickJS does not provide.
smoke: N/A — no buildable/runnable artifact for wasmtime. (If a candidate existed, the smoke would be: `wasmtime run swipl.wasm -- -g "X is 2+3, write(X), nl, halt." -t halt` expecting stdout `5`. The real swipl.wasm cannot run under wasmtime: it imports JS env functions / Emscripten glue and aborts on instantiation with missing imports, and even loaded it needs the JS-driven asyncify/longjmp host loop and a preloaded MEMFS boot image.)
blocker: The sole maintained wasm port is Emscripten-targeted and JS-host-coupled by design: cmake/port/Emscripten.cmake sets SWIPL_ARCH=wasm-emscripten with Emscripten-only -fwasm-exceptions/-sSUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm and an Emscripten MEMFS preload for the Prolog bootstrap; src/wasm/pl-wasm.c uses EM_JS/EM_ASM to call the JS host for I/O and engine yield. Shipped artifact is a .js+swipl.wasm pair (npm swipl-wasm 8.0.0). No wasm32-wasi target, no prebuilt WASI .wasm anywhere (vmware-labs has none), and a from-source build requires CMake/autotools codegen + a native bootstrap-compiler step + emconfigure'd zlib. Engine relies on asyncify/longjmp orchestrated from JS — not provided by bare wasmtime/WASI.
